intent: Hold the iteration 10 geometry (five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to 0.03 in 0.015 m steps, y = 0.04, wheels, body and mass unchanged), which is the best raced design at 74.80. I am not changing the row, forward offset or footprint in this final iteration. Expected result: about 74.8 on the development tracks, with max error near 0.062 m, s-bend oscillation near 0.14 and slalom line loss near 2 per run. The slalom oscillation of 0.246 is the main open risk, and it is the first thing to check if the Integrator has room for a controller-only fix. I am not committing to a forward offset, because it has not been tested cleanly.
learning: Confirmed in iterations 3 to 10: 16 mm footprint edge noise is a contributor to s-bend oscillation, and 12 mm reduces it (0.168 to 0.140) without losing progress. Still open: whether slalom oscillation (0.246) and line loss (1.95 per run) come from sensing lag at the row, from the controller's gain on the sharp slalom bends, or from the start of the course. A forward offset at y = 0.02 to 0.03 remains untested. The off-track limit at max error 0.06 m is the binding failure on every track, and no geometry within range moves it.
rationale:
This is the final iteration, and the design delivered here races on the unseen final track, so the choice is about the most reliable layout rather than another experiment. The best raced design is iteration 10: a 12 mm footprint on the ±0.03 m row at y = 0.04, which scored 74.80, the best of the run. Its per-track results were oval 72.63, s-bend 77.39 and slalom 74.39, with slalom min 55.39.

The 12 mm footprint answered the open question. S-bend steering oscillation fell from 0.168 to 0.140 with progress held at 0.188 to 0.210 and no loss of score, which supports the edge-noise hypothesis for 16 mm. The cost is reach: the outer sensor now covers offsets only to about 0.0485 m, against 0.0505 m at 16 mm. Max error still sits at about 0.062 m on every track, so the 0.06 m off-track limit remains the binding failure, and body width cannot change it within range.

The slalom is the weak point. Steering oscillation rose to 0.246, above the 0.15 trigger I set for a forward offset, and line loss averaged 1.95 per run. I considered moving the row forward to y = 0.02 or 0.03. I did not, because that trigger was written for a single-variable test that has never been run cleanly: the only forward-offset comparison (iteration 0 against 1) also changed the row width. Moving the sensors now would be an untested change applied to the final unseen-track race, where a regression would score directly. The proven 74.80 layout is the safer delivery.

I am therefore holding the iteration 10 geometry exactly. This keeps the Integrator's controller, tuned for this layout, on the platform it was built for, and gives the final race the best measured floor.
